title: When does it snow in Lapland? Snow cover month by month
seoTitle: When does it snow in Lapland? Snow month by month
description: Snow in Lapland: the first snow cover typically comes in October, the snow is deepest in March and April, and it melts in May. Station figures for each month.
dek: In Sodankylä the ground is white for 203 days in an average winter, and the snow is deeper in mid-March than at Christmas. November is the month to plan with care.
heroAlt: A tree bent under a thick load of snow on a hilltop at dusk, with snow-covered spruce forest and a row of lights in the haze below.
heroCaption: A snow-laden tree in Finnish Lapland on 5 January 2012.

body.text: In Finnish Lapland the first snow cover typically arrives in October, the snow is at its deepest from mid-March to early April, and it melts in May. The figures come from the Finnish Meteorological Institute's statistics for 1991–2020.

body.title: Snow in Lapland in brief
items: First snow cover in the north: around 9 and 10 October
First snow cover in Sodankylä, Kuusamo and Rovaniemi: between 18 and 21 October
Deepest snow: from mid-March to early April
Snow melts: in May, and in northernmost Lapland the snow cover lasts until the end of May

body.text: When the first snow comes, place by place
The institute records the first snow cover on the morning a weather station first measures at least 1 cm of snow. Typical dates for 1991–2020, with the earliest and latest since 1961:

items: Kittilä (Pokka, north of Levi): 9 October. Earliest 12 September 1973, latest 1 November 1987.
Utsjoki (Kevo): 10 October. Earliest 18 September 1993, latest 4 November 1987.
Sodankylä: 18 October. Earliest 13 September 1971, latest 17 November 2011.
Kuusamo (Kiutaköngäs): 19 October. Earliest 14 September 1973, latest 5 November 2011.
Rovaniemi (Apukka): 21 October. Earliest 21 September 1968, latest 19 November 2011.

body.text: The first snow often melts away again. Permanent snow cover means the winter's longest unbroken period with at least 1 cm of snow on the ground. Winter, defined by temperature, usually begins in mid-October in Lapland, and permanent snow covers open ground about two weeks later. In Sodankylä the snow cover lasts 203 days in an average winter, about seven months.
How much snow there is, month by month

The depths below are the institute's medians for the 15th of each month in 1991–2020 at two stations: Sodankylä in Central Lapland and Utsjoki Kevo in the far north. They describe the region, not one slope or trail.

items: September: the first snowfalls land on the fell tops, usually in August or September, and melt.
October: the first snow cover arrives across Lapland and often melts again.
November: 13 cm in Sodankylä and 15 cm in Utsjoki in the middle of the month.
December: 33 cm in Sodankylä and 30 cm in Utsjoki. According to the institute, Christmas in Lapland is white practically every year.
January: 53 cm in Sodankylä and 46 cm in Utsjoki.
February: 68 cm in Sodankylä and 59 cm in Utsjoki.
March: 77 cm in Sodankylä and 64 cm in Utsjoki, the highest mid-month values of the winter at both stations.

April: 70 cm in Sodankylä and 60 cm in Utsjoki. In Lapland the snow is often deepest in early April and then melts fast. Finland's snow depth record, 190 cm, was measured in Kilpisjärvi on 19 April 1997.
May: the snow goes. In mid-May the median in Utsjoki is 2 cm, and in northernmost Lapland the snow lasts until the end of the month.

body.text: Does it snow in Lapland in November?

Usually yes, but November varies more from year to year than the months that follow. In 2025 Sodankylä had 29 cm of snow on 15 November, against a median of 13 cm. In 2011 the first snow cover did not arrive in Sodankylä until 17 November and in Rovaniemi until 19 November. In the first half of the month a traveller may find thin snow or bare ground; the later the trip, the better the odds.
Autumn 2026: a warm October, then winter

October 2026 was unusually warm in northern Finland, the Finnish Meteorological Institute said on 2 November. The first snow fell on parts of Central and Northern Lapland in the middle of the month, at the typical time, but at the end of October the whole country was without snow. On 9 November the institute forecast lasting winter for Lapland: frost around the clock, snowfall in the north, and up to 15 cm of new snow in places from Central Lapland southwards by the end of that week.
What this means for timing a trip

items: Christmas trip: snow on the ground is as good as certain in December.
Skiing and snowmobiling: from February to mid-April the mid-month medians at the two stations are between 59 and 77 cm.
Spring snow: March and early April have the deepest snow of the winter. Once thawing begins, night frosts stop the melt until the next day.
Early November: choose activities that do not depend on snow, or go further north, where the first snow cover typically comes earlier than in Rovaniemi.
May: open ground loses its snow two to three weeks after spring begins, and the forests about two weeks later.

body.text: Statistics tell what is typical, not what this winter brings. Before the trip, check the Finnish Meteorological Institute's snow depth observations for your destination and ask the activity operator whether its routes are open.
Each season in Lapland, from the polar night to the midnight sun, is covered in our seasons guide.

body.text: The dark months of the snow season are also the time for the northern lights.
